name: Electric-Assisted Bicycle
description: A two- or three-wheeled bicycle with a saddle, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of not more than 750 watts, in class 1, 2 or 3 or a switchable multiple-mode combination of them. Defined by Minnesota Statutes §169.011, subd. 27 (last amended in 2024) and regulated by §169.222, subds. 6a and 6b.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; class 2 can propel it without pedaling and stops at 20 mph; class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
A multiple-mode e-bike has switchable or programmable modes that let it operate as two or more of the classes
Its battery or electric drive system must be tested to a safety standard by a third-party laboratory
Not an electric-assisted bicycle if it's designed or sold to be configured or modified out of these limits
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Riders must be 15 or older, for every class
Excluded from the definition of motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including road shoulders, bike lanes and bicycle routes
Class 1 and 2 may use bicycle and shared-use paths with the motor on unless the DNR or managing agency prohibits it for safety
Class 3 and multiple-mode e-bikes may use bicycle and shared-use paths with the motor on unless the local authority or agency over the path prohibits it
On a natural-surface trail or bike park designated nonmotorized, the managing agency may regulate it
Kept off sidewalks in a business district unless local authorities permit it
